name: Anthropic
summary: Claude's enterprise momentum, compute economics, and the race to build a lasting AI business.
overview: Anthropic's business case rests on valuable professional use, especially coding and enterprise work. Claude's growth and major technology partnerships support that case, while the company must keep investing heavily in compute and research as competition intensifies.

facts.label: IPO status
facts.note: Anthropic filed an amended registration statement on November 2, 2026. The offering price, share count, and listing date remain undisclosed.

facts.label: Latest valuation
facts.note: Series H post-money valuation announced May 28, 2026

facts.label: Latest funding
facts.note: Series H led by Altimeter, Dragoneer, Greenoaks, and Sequoia

facts.label: Revenue
facts.note: Nine months ended September 30, 2026, up 1,206% year over year.

facts.note: Nine months ended September 30, 2026, compared with a $5.22 billion operating loss in the prior-year period.

facts.note: 12% adjusted operating margin for the nine months ended September 30, 2026. This is a company-defined non-GAAP measure.

facts.label: Cash and short-term investments
facts.note: $95.6 billion of cash and cash equivalents plus $36.3 billion of short-term investments as of September 30, 2026.

facts.label: Operating cash flow

facts.note: Aggregate committed spend for purchase commitments and leases, substantially all related to compute and infrastructure. $447.5 billion is expected before 2030 and $69.8 billion is due within 12 months.

facts.note: Customers with at least $100,000 of trailing-12-month revenue as of September 30, 2026. The filing also reports 1,900+ customers above $1 million and about 250 above $10 million.

facts.label: Net revenue retention
facts.note: Company-defined metric as of September 30, 2026, excluding fixed-price Claude subscriptions.

facts.label: Top-five customer share
facts.note: Share of revenue from the top five customers for the nine months ended September 30, 2026; no single customer exceeded 10%.

bull_case: The S-1/A shows rapidly expanding enterprise adoption, revenue, and operating cash generation, which could support a durable software and services business.
bear_case: Nearly $895 billion of compute and infrastructure commitments, intense competition, and safety constraints may keep margins and differentiation under pressure.
directory_notes: Model quality and unit economics are the key variables.

intelligence.description: Anthropic develops Claude, an AI assistant and model platform used across consumer, developer, and enterprise workflows.
company: Anthropic is a public benefit corporation founded in 2021 by former OpenAI leaders. It develops Claude, a family of foundation models and products positioned around reliable, steerable AI for professional and enterprise use.

The commercial story is increasingly tied to coding, knowledge work, and API adoption. Its S-1/A reported $33.2 billion of revenue in the first nine months of 2026, alongside substantial investment and long-dated commitments for compute and infrastructure.
intelligence.why_it_matters: Anthropic's S-1/A makes the trade-off behind frontier AI unusually visible: rapid revenue and enterprise adoption against extraordinary compute obligations. Its demand for cloud capacity, chips, and enterprise software distribution affects Amazon, Google, Microsoft, Nvidia, and the broader AI supply chain, while the eventual IPO will test whether public investors support that capital intensity.

changed.text: Anthropic is founded by former OpenAI leaders, with a public-benefit structure and a focus on AI safety.
Claude enters the market and Anthropic expands its cloud distribution through strategic partnerships.
Enterprise adoption accelerates, pushing the company into the top tier of private AI companies by valuation.
Anthropic files an S-1/A for a proposed Nasdaq listing under ANT, disclosing financial results, enterprise adoption, and large compute commitments.

takeaways: Claude's strength in professional and coding workflows gives Anthropic a commercially valuable enterprise position.
The company is scaling with unusually deep dependencies on cloud, chips, and hyperscale infrastructure partners.
The S-1/A reports $33.2 billion of nine-month revenue and 11,900+ customers with at least $100,000 of trailing-12-month revenue.
The $895.4 billion disclosed compute and infrastructure commitment makes capital intensity central to the long-term case.
The IPO registration is public, but a price, share count, valuation, and listing date are still not disclosed.
